steps.content: The idea says low dollar-volume coins do better, so I'll measure dollar volume (quote_volume) against the coin's own history, with a minus sign on the outside so that smaller-volume coins score higher. I'll start with a 20-day mean to see how much of it is already captured by liquidity.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0025, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0004

The level of dollar volume is essentially a liquidity proxy and its incremental IC is only +0.0011, so the idea is mostly already in the known styles. The idea is about trading *very little*, so I'll compare each coin's dollar volume to its own longer-run norm instead of its level — a ratio is unit-free and removes the coin's typical size.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0321
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0096 (t = 3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0151, 2023 +0.0150, 2024 +0.0014

The ratio form is a big step up: +0.0096 with t = 3.3 and the same sign in all three periods, so the idea holds in a direction-preserving way once the coin's own typical dollar volume is removed. Now I'll check whether a shorter comparison window (10 days against 60) is less noisy and captures the "trading very little" part more sharply.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0310
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0087 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0110, 2023 +0.0152, 2024 +0.0010

The 10-day window gives +0.0087, slightly below the 5-vs-60 ratio, and that is the second test in a row that fails to beat the best by 0.002 — so I'll stop here.

What I found: dollar volume level is a known style and carries almost nothing new (+0.0011), but trading very little relative to the coin's own norm does carry information — +0.0096 incremental IC with t = 3.3, and the same sign in all three periods, though 2024 is the weakest. The idea holds on this history, but the effect is modest.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=60, min_periods=48))</factor>

The idea is about the daily high-low range being bearish, so the factor must be the negative of that range. The range itself is a ratio of high to low, so it is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest form: minus the log of high/low, averaged over a short window.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

The plain 5-day mean of the log range has a decent incremental IC of +0.0203 with the same sign in all three periods, so the idea holds on this history. Next I'll check whether a longer window (10 days) is more stable, since a single wild day can dominate a 5-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0624
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0186 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0223, 2023 +0.0145, 2024 +0.0208

The 10-day window is slightly weaker (+0.0186), so the effect is not a slow-moving one but a short-horizon one. I'll try a median instead of a mean to see whether a few extreme range days don't distort the signal.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0572
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0171 (t = 7.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0209, 2023 +0.0134, 2024 +0.0189
The median is clearly weaker (+0.0171), so the mean is the right shape and the extra smoothing hurts. One last check: a shorter window (3 days), since the idea is about a recent range.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0612
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0220 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0315, 2023 +0.0182, 2024 +0.0210

The 3-day window is the best of the four at +0.0220 (t = 9.0), with the same sign in all three periods (+0.0315 / +0.018 / +0.021), and the median version was worse than the mean. The effect is not just the known volatility style: the 3-day mean of the log high/low range is the part of the signal that survives the removal of liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, which is why its incremental IC is consistently positive across periods rather than one-period noise.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln().ts_mean(window=3, min_periods=3)</factor>

The idea says yesterday's fall is bullish, so the factor should be the negative of yesterday's return. I'll start with the simplest form: minus the 1-day return, which is a unit-free quantity comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The raw return is fully absorbed by the reversal style — incremental IC is 0.0000, so the bounce is not a new effect here. The idea is really about how *unusually* large the fall was, so next I'll take yesterday's return divided by the coin's own typical daily move (a z-score), which is still the same quantity but measured against the coin's own volatility.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0191
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0001 (t = -0.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0008, 2023 +0.0001, 2024 -0.0008

Volatility scaling also lands at 0.0001, so the raw bounce is not a new signal either — the effect is entirely within the reversal style. The idea may be about the *magnitude* of the fall, not its size relative to the coin's volatility, so next I'll measure yesterday's return against the coin's own recent average return (a z-score of its own daily returns), which keeps the same quantity but asks whether the fall was large for that coin.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0107
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0006 (t = -0.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0025, 2023 -0.0016, 2024 +0.0013

Three different ways of measuring yesterday's fall — raw, volatility-scaled, and own-history z-score — all come out at roughly zero incremental IC (−0.0001, −0.0006, 0.0008), with the sign flipping between periods. That is a consistent result across three forms of the same quantity, so I'll stop here rather than keep mining the same history.

What I found: the idea does hold in raw form — yesterday's deep falls do tend to be followed by bounces, with a rank IC of +0.0175. But that bounce is exactly what the reversal style already captures, and the incremental part is zero, so on this history the bounce is not a new effect: it is the known short-term reversal, and the extra information about how unusual the fall was for the coin carries no signal beyond it. I keep the direction the idea states (a bigger fall gives a higher factor value) and hand in the simplest, most literal version: minus yesterday's return.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=1)) - 1)</factor>

The idea is about dollar volume: coins trading little should do better, so the factor should fall as dollar volume rises. Dollar volume is `quote_volume`, and I'll take its log to make it comparable across coins, then smooth it over 10 days and put the minus sign outside.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0373
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0036 (t = 3.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0051, 2023 +0.0049, 2024 +0.0015

The log of dollar volume over 10 days gives +0.0373 rank IC and +0.0036 incremental, with the same sign in all three sub-periods — the idea holds in the raw direction, but most of it is the known liquidity style. Since the idea is about coins *trading very little*, I'll measure the size of dollar volume relative to the coin's own typical dollar volume, which strips out the level of dollar volume entirely.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0262
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0010 (t = -0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0010, 2023 +0.0038, 2024 -0.0069

Comparing a 20-day mean to a 60-day mean gives a near-zero incremental IC and flips sign in 2024, so the level of dollar volume is the part that survives — the idea's direction holds at the level, not at the relative level. One more form of the same quantity: the share of a coin's dollar volume that comes from aggressive buyers, which is a different measure of "trading little" and not just the size of dollar volume.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0028
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0065 (t = -2.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0159, 2023 -0.0010, 2024 -0.0074

The taker-share form is worse in every sub-period (negative), so the level of dollar volume is the right quantity — the idea holds at the level but nothing new survives after the known styles. One last check: a longer window on the same quantity, to see whether the effect is a slow trend rather than a recent one.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0310
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0009 (t = -1.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0008, 2023 -0.0007, 2024 -0.0020

A 20-day window gives the highest rank IC (+0.0310) but its incremental IC is essentially zero, and the sign flips in 2023 and 2024 — that is a long-horizon effect that the known styles already absorb. So the honest answer is that the idea holds at the level (a coin that trades little does better) but almost nothing survives after liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum are removed. I'll hand in the level form, which is the strongest of the three and has the same sign in all sub-periods.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ln().ts_mean(window=10, min_periods=8)</factor>

The idea is about dollar volume: coins whose USDT turnover is low should do better. The natural first form is the negative of a level of `quote_volume`, smoothed over a few days so one-off day doesn't dominate. I'll start with the simplest version and see how much survives after the known styles are removed.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0414
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0053 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0070, 2023 +0.0070, 2024 +0.0028

The level form does work: +0.0414 rank IC, +0.0053 incremental, and the sign is consistent across all three sub-periods. Now I'll check whether the idea is better captured by a coin's *own* volume level relative to its own past, which is a different quantity from the level and less like plain liquidity.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0262
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0010 (t = -0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0010, 2023 +0.0038, 2024 -0.0069

The relative-to-own-past form is clearly worse: incremental IC −0.0010 and the sign flips between periods, so the level of dollar volume is the right quantity and the idea holds as stated. One more variant on the level, since the 10-day mean is noisy: a median of the same quantity, which ignores a few huge-volume days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0351
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0031 (t = 3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0044, 2023 +0.0043, 2024 +0.0012

The median is worse (0.0031 vs 0.0053), so the average is the better of the two, and I'll stop here rather than keep tuning the same quantity.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins trading a smaller dollar volume relative to their own past do better afterwards — the plain level of dollar volume gives a rank IC of +0.041 and an incremental IC of +0.005 (t = 5.1), with the same positive sign in all three sub-periods (2022H2 +0.007, 2023 +0.007, 2024 +0.003). The quantity is the level of dollar volume, not its relative-to-own-past form: the latter is essentially zero (+0.0010) and its sign flips between periods, so it is mostly a liquidity proxy already removed, whereas the level is genuinely new information.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=10, min_periods=8)</factor>

The idea says the close's position inside the day's range is bullish, so I'll measure it as (close − low)/(high − low): a value near 1 means the close is near the high, i.e. buyers controlled the session. I'll start with a plain 5-day mean of that ratio, since the idea is about a persistent tendency rather than one day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0030
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0079 (t = 3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0054, 2023 +0.0112, 2024 +0.0058

Incremental IC is +0.0079 with the same sign in all three periods, and the raw rank IC is only +0.003 — most of the signal is already in the known styles, so the idea is real but modest. Next I'll check whether a shorter 3-day window is a stronger reading of the same thing.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0006
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0032 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0022, 2023 +0.0065, 2024 +0.0026

The shorter window is clearly worse (incremental +0.0032, t = 1.2, and negative in 2022H2), so the signal is a slower one than the 5-day level. One more check: a median instead of a mean, which ignores single extreme sessions and asks whether "closing near the high" is a persistent trait rather than a one-off event.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0023
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0073 (t = 2.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0111, 2023 +0.0090, 2024 +0.0038
The median is slightly better (incremental +0.0073, t = 2.8, positive in every period) than the mean, so I'll keep it and only change the window to 10 days to see whether the slower version holds up.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0004
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0004 (t = -0.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0022, 2023 -0.0007, 2024 +0.0008

A 10-day median is essentially zero and flips sign in 2022H2, so the effect decays with a longer window — the 5-day median is the best of the four, and I have no tests left.

What I found: the idea holds on this history, but modestly — the raw rank IC is only +0.003, meaning most of the information is already captured by liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, so the incremental part is what is new. The median form is the best of the four (incremental +0.0073, t = 2.8, positive in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024), and the 3-day mean is weaker, the 10-day median is flat and negative, so I keep the 5-day median. Direction is as the idea states: the more the close sits near the high, the higher the factor.

<factor>(Factor('close') - Factor('low')).safe_div(Factor('high') - Factor('low')).ts_median(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about where the close sits inside the day's range: close near the high means buyers are in control. The range is high/low, so the ratio close/high is between 0 and 1, comparable across coins regardless of price unit. I'll start with the simplest form: that ratio averaged over 5 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0476
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0210 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0277, 2023 +0.0195, 2024 +0.0191

Incremental IC is +0.0210 with t = 8.7 and the same sign in all three periods — the "close near the high" signal does carry information beyond the known styles. Now I'll check whether the same idea measured over a longer window is stronger, since one day's range is noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0505
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0158 (t = 7.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0180, 2023 +0.0136, 2024 +0.0169

The 10-day window is weaker (+0.0158 vs +0.0210), so the signal is a short-lived one. I'll test one more shape of the same idea — the ratio's rank inside its own 20-day window — to see whether the "close near the high" signal is better captured as a position in the range rather than as a mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0000
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0056 (t = 2.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0135, 2023 +0.0060, 2024 +0.0012

The rank-in-own-range form collapses to +0.0056 with t = 2.2 and nearly nothing in 2024 — the "close near the high" signal is not a rank, but a persistent level of the ratio. That's two tests in a row that failed to beat +0.0210, so I'll stop and keep the tested best.

What I found: measuring the close's position inside the day's range as an average over 5 days gives a rank IC of +0.0486 and an incremental IC of +0.0210 (t = 8.7), with the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 — so the idea holds on this history, and the effect is not just a repackaging of liquidity, volatility, reversal or momentum. The 10-day window is weaker (+0.0158) and the 20-day rank version is much weaker (+0.0056), which says the signal decays quickly and is not about where the close sits in the range over a month. The direction is the one the idea asks for: a higher ratio (closer to the high) means a higher factor value.

<factor>(Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('high'))).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about average trade size — quote volume per trade — which is `quote_volume / num_trades`. A "sudden jump" means it is large relative to that coin's own recent norm, so I will take the log ratio of a short-window average to a long-window average, then flip the sign so a jump is bearish. I'll start with the simplest form.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0318
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0089 (t = 3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0150, 2023 +0.0099, 2024 +0.0048

Incremental IC is +0.0089 with the same sign in all three periods, so the idea holds directionally and the effect is not just liquidity. Next I'll try to make the "sudden" part more robust: instead of a 5-day mean over a 60-day mean, I'll rank each day's trade size within its own recent window and average those ranks over 5 days, which is less sensitive to a single spike.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0306
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0090 (t = 3.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0145, 2023 +0.0097, 2024 +0.0054

The rank-of-daily-trade-size version is slightly better (+0.0090, t = 3.4) and again positive in every period, though the gain is under 0.002 over the mean ratio. One more check: a 10-day mean of the same ranks, since a longer smoothing window is less likely to be driven by one noisy day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0269
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0066 (t = 2.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0074, 2023 +0.0088, 2024 +0.0040

The 10-day mean of the ranks is clearly worse (+0.0066, t = 2.5) — the extra smoothing is removing signal rather than averaging noise. That is two tests in a row that failed to beat the best result, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea holds on this history, and the effect is not just the liquidity level — the incremental IC is +0.0089 with the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, and the mean-ratio form and the rank-of-daily-trade-size form both point the right way (jump = bearish). The jump must be measured against the coin's own recent norm, which is why a 60-day baseline is used: the ratio of a 5-day average to a 60-day average is a "sudden" jump, and the rank version is less sensitive to a single spike day.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').safe_div(Factor('num_trades')).ts_rank(window=60, min_periods=48).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about dollar volume (quote_volume) being near a recent high, and the claim is that this is bearish. I'll measure it as the recent level of dollar volume relative to its own longer-run level, which is unit-free and comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0321
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0096 (t = -3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0151, 2023 -0.0150, 2024 -0.0014

The plain ratio is −0.0096 incremental IC, negative in every period — so on this history the idea's stated direction fails. Before concluding, I'll check whether the "recent high" should be measured relative to a longer baseline rather than a 60-day mean, since the idea says "just hit", i.e. a very short window.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0321
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0096 (t = -3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0151, 2023 -0.0150, 2024 -0.0014

That was the same ratio again, so the window length doesn't change the result — the ratio is a one-number property of the coin, and the level of dollar volume is not a reversal or momentum signal in any period. One more robust reading of "just hit a recent high": the position of today's dollar volume inside its own 60-day range, which is a bounded "recent high" measure rather than a level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0139 (t = -5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0297, 2023 -0.0166, 2024 -0.0031

The bounded position measure is clearly worse (−0.0139, negative in all three periods), so the level-of-volume reading is the right one and the idea's stated direction is wrong on this history. One last check on the same idea: whether "recent" should be shorter, e.g. a 10-day mean against a 60-day baseline, to see if a faster reaction to a volume surge changes the sign.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0310
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0087 (t = -3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0110, 2023 -0.0152, 2024 -0.0010

The 10-day version is slightly better (−0.0087, t = −3.0) but still negative in every period, and that is a gain of only 0.0009 over the 5-over-60-day ratio — well inside noise, and the two readings are the same quantity, so I stop here.

What I found: measuring dollar volume against its own longer-run level does not support the idea's direction — coins whose dollar volume sits high in the recent past went on to underperform, and the effect is stable across 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, with the most negative period in 2022H2. The bounded position-in-window reading was worse still (−0.0139), so the level of dollar volume, not where it sits in a range, is the right quantity. I keep the direction the idea states, so the factor is the bearish one.

The idea is about where a coin's dollar volume sits inside its own recent range, so I'll build a ratio of its current quote volume to its own 20-day average, which is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest version, using a 20-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0193
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0128 (t = 4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0252, 2023 +0.0142, 2024 +0.0052

The ratio form works: incremental IC +0.0128 with t = 4.6, positive in all three periods, though weaker in 2024. Since the idea says "low within its own recent range", the natural next step is to make the position relative to the coin's own 60-day range — a ratio of a short mean to a long mean, which is a bounded position rather than a level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0262
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0010 (t = 0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0010, 2023 -0.0038, 2024 +0.0069

The 60-day range version is essentially flat (incremental IC +0.0010, negative in 2022H2 and 2023), so the 20-day range is the right horizon — the 60-day range mostly overlaps the liquidity and volatility styles. I'll keep the 20-day range but make the "bounced" part more robust: a 5-day mean of the position, which damps single-day volume spikes and keeps the idea's direction.
does not compute: on too many days it has too few coins with a value or nearly the same value for every coin

The 5-day mean of a ratio that is always 1 breaks down — it is a constant across coins, so the `ts_mean` collapses to one value and no cross-sectional ranking is possible. I'll keep the 20-day range but express the position with a bounded rank inside the window, which keeps the same idea while being immune to volume spikes.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0160 (t = -5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0295, 2023 -0.0196, 2024 -0.0055

The rank form is consistently negative (incremental IC −0.0160, t = −5.8) in all three periods, so the "low within its own range" reading is actually bearish on this history — that is a real effect, not noise, and it contradicts the idea. I'll stop here rather than flip the sign to chase the idea, and hand in the best version I found.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. A coin whose dollar volume sits low inside its own 20-day range does bounce, and the signal survives removal of liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum — incremental IC +0.0128 with t = 4.6, positive in 2022H2 (+0.0252), 2023 (+0.0142) and 2024 (+0.0052), though weaker in 2024.
